title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 Trends in Australia
description: Australian interest in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 is on the rise as semiconductor sell-off impacts the markets.

sources.title: Nasdaq 100 nears a correction as semiconductor sell-off extends
Chipmakers falling into bear market offset by gains in Coca-Cola and Boeing
‘A lot of panic around the AI investment’: How a chip slump is driving the Nasdaq toward correction

sections.heading: Market Overview
paragraphs: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 are significant stock market indices that have recently been trending in Australia. The S&P 500, which includes 500 leading companies listed on US stock exchanges, and the Nasdaq 100, comprising the 100 largest non-financial companies on the Nasdaq stock market, are key indicators of market performance.

sections.heading: Recent Market Developments
paragraphs: According to AFR, the Nasdaq 100 is nearing a correction as the semiconductor sell-off extends. This indicates a significant shift in the market, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 being particularly affected by the decline in semiconductor stocks.

News.com.au reports that while chipmakers are falling into a bear market, gains in companies like Coca-Cola and Boeing are helping to offset these losses. This suggests a mixed performance across different sectors, with some stocks providing stability amidst the overall market volatility.

sections.heading: Impact on AI Investment
paragraphs: Yahoo Finance Australia discusses the impact of the chip slump on AI investment, noting that there is 'a lot of panic around the AI investment'. The downturn in the semiconductor market is driving the Nasdaq toward a correction, which could have broader implications for technology and AI-focused investments.

faq.a: The S&P 500 is a stock market index that tracks the performance of 500 leading companies listed on US stock exchanges.
The Nasdaq 100 is a stock market index consisting of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq stock market.
Semiconductor stocks are crucial as they are a key component of the technology sector, impacting various industries including AI and technology-focused investments.

faq.q: What does a market correction mean?
faq.a: A market correction refers to a decline of at least 10% from the recent peak in a stock market index, indicating a significant shift in market sentiment and performance.
